# @handamade/psi-react

46 React 19 components consuming @handamade/psi-tokens. Zero runtime deps, CSS Modules, ref-as-prop.

## Machine-readable artifacts
- dist/manifest.json: full component/prop inventory with types and defaults
- dist/patterns.json: 22 composition patterns (D47) — gap-annotated recipes with clarifying parameters; presets are generated JSX, never hand-written
- docs/{Component}.md: per-component docs (props, theming, variant guidance)

## Rules for generated code
- import { Button } from "@handamade/psi-react"; import "@handamade/psi-react/styles";
- Also import from @handamade/psi-tokens: base.css, a theme css, components.css, utilities.css.
- size is a px number (24|32|40|48), never "sm"/"md"/"lg".
- variant vocabulary: accent | accent-subtle | neutral | neutral-subtle | ghost | danger | danger-subtle | outline.
- One accent per visual group. danger only for destructive actions.
- Every focusable part Psi renders draws one focus ring on `:focus-visible` (D82). For your own focusable element, bind the same tokens rather than writing a literal: `outline: var(--psi-focus-ring-width) solid var(--psi-border-focus); outline-offset: var(--psi-focus-ring-offset)` (or `--psi-focus-ring-offset-inset` to draw it inside). Never `outline: none`.
- Before composing multi-component UI, consult dist/patterns.json (or psi-mcp search) for a matching pattern and honor its clarifying parameters; presets are copy-paste JSX generated from the compose tree.
- Pattern `content` text in `[square brackets]` is a placeholder to replace with real copy. Never `<angle brackets>` or `{braces}` — those do not parse as JSX text, so the build rejects them (D48 class 9).

## Button: href + outline (D33/D34)
- Button renders as an <a> when given `href` (plus optional `target`/`rel`); disabled anchors get aria-disabled, no href attribute, and pointer-events: none instead of the disabled attribute.
- `outline` is a bordered-ghost variant: visible structure, no fill until hover — good for marketing CTAs and download buttons.
- --psi-button-font overrides button typography across all sizes in one declaration; brands can set it via componentOverrides (ember → mono).

## Card
- <Card variant="stacked" | "featured" media={...} hoverLift>: stacked places media above the body, featured places media beside it (~1.6fr/1fr, stacks under the md breakpoint). hoverLift lifts the card translateY(-6px) over --psi-duration-350. Border uses --psi-border-faint.

## Panel
- <Panel padding={16|24}>: the elevated surface panel (D51) — bg-secondary, faint hairline border, radius-12, space-24 padding (16 for compact). Binds the shared --psi-surface-* recipe Dialog's panel also uses; brands retune both by overriding --psi-surface-*. Not a Card: no media slot, no hover lift.

## DescriptionList (2)
- `<DescriptionList layout="stacked|inline" gap={8|12|16}>` with one `<DescriptionItem term="Date">value</DescriptionItem>` per field (D70). Renders `<dl>`; each item is a `<div><dt/><dd/></div>` group, which is the HTML5 grouping element, so the term/value association survives.
- `stacked` (default) puts the term above its value; `inline` is a two-column grid and is what a detail drawer wants. This is the body of the `detail-drawer` pattern — do not hand-roll a `<dl>`.
- The term is a prop and the value is children, matching Field's `label` idiom. No `size` prop: this is type, so restyle through `--psi-description-list-*`.

## Toolbar
- <Toolbar gap={8|12|16} aria-label="Filters">: horizontal wrapping row for filter/search controls (Input, Select, Tag, Button). Wraps on overflow (D52); with aria-label it announces as role=group. Deliberately not ARIA role=toolbar (no roving tabindex). Unblocks the filter-toolbar pattern — consult dist/patterns.json for the preset.
- `align="end"` lines items up on their bottom edge, so Field-wrapped controls (label above) and a button without a label share one control line (D87). It aligns each item's last line: a Field in that row must end on its control — no description or error under it.
- `as="form"` renders a real `<form>`: a `Button type="submit"` and Enter in a field submit it; wire `onSubmit`. With `aria-label` it is a named form landmark (no role=group). Filters that apply as they change, named by aria-label → filter-toolbar; labelled filters submitted together with *Find* → filter-form. Never name a control by its placeholder alone.

## NavBar
- <NavBar brand={...} actions={...}>{links}</NavBar>: brand slot leading, nav links centered/inline, actions slot trailing (theme switch, CTA). Renders inside .psi-container. Background defaults to --psi-scrim-heavy so content can scroll underneath; border uses --psi-border-faint.
- `navLabel` names the links' `<nav>` (rest props land on `<header>`, so it cannot be labelled any other way). `<nav>` renders only when there are children: a brand-and-actions bar has no empty landmark, and `actions` keeps the trailing edge. `fluid` drops .psi-container for a full-width row that keeps the `--psi-gutter` side padding — an application header (D88).

## SkipLink
- <SkipLink href="#main">Skip to content</SkipLink>: a plain anchor, no script, render it first in the document. Invisible until it takes keyboard focus, then fixed at the inline-start top corner on a surface with the shared focus ring. Fragment navigation moves focus only to a focusable target — give `<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>` (AppShell's main will be one). A modal Dialog makes it inert; do not place a ToastRegion at `top-start` in an app with a skip link, because the top layer paints over it (D88).

## AspectRatio
- <AspectRatio ratio={16/10}>{children}</AspectRatio>: a frame div with CSS aspect-ratio set from the numeric ratio prop — wrap images/media to reserve layout space before load. Combine with the .psi-media-tint utility for the brand media-tint treatment.

## Icons (26)
- Full icon set: IconPlus, IconMinus, IconCheck, IconClose, IconChevronDown, IconChevronRight, IconSearch, IconSettings, IconUser, IconEye, IconEyeOff, IconEdit, IconCopy, IconTrash, IconLoader, IconExternalLink, plus D36 additions — arrows IconArrowDown and IconArrowUpRight, and social glyphs IconLinkedIn, IconGitHub, IconX, IconInstagram — plus the D64 status glyphs IconInfo, IconAlertTriangle and IconAlertCircle, and the D70 IconMoreHorizontal — the ellipsis glyph for a row-actions trigger.

## Table family (7)
- `<Table>` renders `<table>` and is **controlled-only** — it holds no state (D62). Sorting is `sort={{key, direction}}` + `onSortChange`, which is called with the **next** state, already toggled — store it as given (a fresh column arrives `asc`; an active `asc` emits `desc`); selection is `selected` (a `ReadonlySet<string>` keyed by each `<TableRow rowId>`) + `onSelectionChange`. `sortable` and `selectable` only enable the affordances. `size` is `32 | 40 | 48` px (default 40) and `stickyHeader` pins the header. It does no filtering, sorting or slicing of rows — the consumer does that.
- `<TableHead>`, `<TableBody>`, `<TableRow>` render `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`. `<TableHeaderCell>` renders `<th scope="col">`, taking `sortKey` to become sortable and putting `aria-sort` on the `<th>`. `<TableCell>` renders `<td>`. Both cells take `numeric`, which right-aligns **and** renders tabular figures.
- `<TableCaption detail="Rows 51–100 of more than 100,000">Applications</TableCaption>` renders `<caption>` as the table's first child — its visible name, plus a `detail` line for the range (D85). For a token-paged list give it `tabIndex={-1}` and move focus to it (through its `ref`) after a page change, so the new range is read. `<TableCell colSpan={n}>` spans an empty-state row; `<TableCell rowHeader>` renders `<th scope="row">` for the cell that names its row. Every family member spreads its remaining attributes onto its element (`aria-busy` on `TableBody` while a page loads, `aria-label`, `id`, `data-*`) and takes a `ref`; its own attributes (`data-size`, `scope`, `aria-sort`) win.
- Selecting rows: give each `<TableRow>` a `rowId` and a `selectLabel` — the row checkbox has no visible label, so `selectLabel` is its accessible name. `<TableHead>` grows the select-all checkbox automatically; do not add one. Consult dist/patterns.json for the `data-table` pattern.

## Pagination and CursorPagination
- `<Pagination page={n} pageCount={total} onPageChange={...}>`: a numbered pager with ellipsis truncation (`‹ 1 … 4 5 6 … 13 ›`), built from Button/IconButton (D63). `siblingCount` (default 1) sets how many pages flank the current one before truncating; `aria-current="page"` marks the active page and the ellipsis is inert. `page` outside `[1, pageCount]` (including non-finite values) is clamped for rendering and warns in development (D78).
- It is **standalone, not a Table family member** and has no connection to `Table` — `Table` has no `page` prop. The `table-pagination` pattern composes it as a `Toolbar` sibling of a page-size `Select`; the consumer owns page state and slices the rows.
- `<CursorPagination hasPrevious hasNext onPrevious={...} onNext={...}>` is the pager for a list that pages by opaque token — a backend returning a `nextPageToken`, no page count (D85). A `<nav>` of two ghost Buttons with **visible words**, *Previous* and *Next* (`previousLabel`/`nextLabel` to translate, `aria-label` for the nav), each with a chevron that only reinforces the word; an unavailable direction is disabled. It holds no state: the consumer holds the tokens. Not a mode of `Pagination`, which needs a page count. Consult dist/patterns.json for the `cursor-pagination` pattern, and pair it with a `TableCaption` that states the range.

## Dialog, and drawers (there is no Drawer component)
- `<Dialog open onClose={(reason) => …} title footer width={400|560|720} dismissible>`: modal on the native `<dialog>` top layer. **Controlled-only** (D50) — every dismissal path (`"esc"`, `"backdrop"`, `"close-button"`) only *reports* via `onClose(reason)`; the consumer flips `open`. `dismissible={false}` swallows Esc and backdrop, leaving the footer as the only exit.
- **A drawer / side sheet is `<Dialog placement="inline-end">`, not a separate component (D66).** `placement` is `center | inline-start | inline-end`; the `inline-*` values pin the panel full-height to that edge. Do not import `Drawer` — it does not exist and never will. `width` is then the drawer's width; the height is always the viewport.
- Placement changes position and nothing else: modality, the focus trap, `aria-modal`, focus restore and the dismissal reasons are identical. Logical (`inline-*`, not left/right), so RTL flips for free. Consult dist/patterns.json for the `detail-drawer` pattern.

## Feedback (4)
- `<Banner variant="neutral|success|warning|danger" title action onDismiss statusLabel>message</Banner>` is **not a live region** (D86): a page-level message, full width, above the content. It shows the message and announces nothing; speak the same event through the announcer. Same status vocabulary as Toast; `action` takes a ghost Button, `onDismiss` renders a labelled Dismiss button, `statusLabel` replaces or drops the hidden status word. Consult dist/patterns.json for `page-banner`.
- `<InlineAlert variant title>message</InlineAlert>` is **not a live region** (D86), and despite its name it is **not `role="alert"`**: a message inside content, bordered in the variant's foreground colour. Put it above a form after a rejected submission and speak the result separately. Consult dist/patterns.json for `form-feedback`.
- `<Skeleton>` is **not a live region** (D86): a loading placeholder that is always `aria-hidden`, so it says nothing. Put `aria-busy` on the region it stands in for (a `TableBody`, a list) — that is what assistive tech reads. The shimmer stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Consult dist/patterns.json for `loading-table`.
- `<CopyButton value label size onCopy>` is **not a live region** (D86): a Button with a visible label that copies `value` to the clipboard and reports `"copied" | "failed"` through `onCopy`. It never changes its label or icon and announces nothing; speak the result through the announcer or a Toast. Consult dist/patterns.json for `copyable-id`.

## Toast family (4) + useToast
- `<Toast variant="neutral|success|warning|danger" action={...} onDismiss={...}>message</Toast>` is presentational and **controlled** (D64): it holds no state, runs no timer and never removes itself — `onDismiss` reports and the owner disposes. Variants are Tag's **status** axis, not the flat action variants; there is deliberately no `accent`. The variant's meaning is announced by a visually hidden status word, so never rely on the icon colour alone; `statusLabel="Fehler:"` replaces that word with a translated one and `statusLabel={null}` drops it (D83).
- `<ToastRegion placement="bottom-end">` is the positioned container and must wrap every toast. It renders **two always-present live wrappers** (`role="status"` polite, `role="alert"` assertive) and routes each child into one: by its `politeness` prop when it names one, otherwise by variant — neutral/success polite, warning/danger assertive. Set `politeness="assertive"` on a success toast when the outcome of the user's own action should interrupt (D83). Whatever it holds, the region is exactly two live regions. Other HTML attributes, `data-*` included, land on its root element: mark it `data-react-aria-top-layer` if the app uses React Aria overlays, or they hide it. It sits on the native top layer via `popover="manual"`, so a toast raised from inside a modal `Dialog` is still painted above the backdrop and still announced — though not clickable until the dialog closes, since `showModal()` makes everything outside the dialog inert. Raise toasts *after* the dialog closes if they carry an `action`.
- `<ToastProvider limit={3} duration={5000} actionDuration={10000}>` owns the queue, the timers and the single region — the library's **one stateful container** (D65), and opt-in. Inside it, `const toast = useToast()` gives `show({variant, message, action, politeness, statusLabel}) => id`, `dismiss(id)` and `clear()`. Timers pause while the pointer or focus is in the region and resume with the time remaining (WCAG 2.2.1); toasts carrying an action get the longer lifetime.
- `<Announcement politeness="polite|assertive">text</Announcement>` is **not a live region** (D83). It is visually hidden text that `ToastRegion` places in its polite (default) or assertive wrapper — for an event that must be spoken and has nothing to show, such as a state change of the object on screen, or field errors the form already displays. It renders no `role` and no `aria-live`, so outside a `ToastRegion` it announces nothing: never use it as a second announcer. It never removes itself; remove it once spoken, and to announce the same text again render it again with a new `key`. Consult dist/patterns.json for the `announcer` pattern.
- **Do not hand-roll a queue or a `setTimeout`** — that is what `ToastProvider` is for. Do not render a bare `<Toast>` outside a `ToastRegion`: it would announce nothing. `useToast()` throws outside a provider rather than silently doing nothing.

## NavTree family (3)
- `<NavTree aria-label="Main">` is a `<nav>` around a `<ul>` of `<NavItem>` and `<NavGroup>` (D88). `aria-label` is **required**: an app has more than one navigation landmark. It is native and router-agnostic — **Tab** moves through group buttons and the links of open groups; there is no roving tabindex, no arrow keys and no `role="menu"` or `role="tree"`.
- `<NavItem>` is an `<li>` that styles the one anchor inside it: pass your router's link. `current` clones that single child with `aria-current="page"` (D93); without `current` the child's own `aria-current` is left alone, so a router that marks its active link keeps working. The current page shows by weight, a raised surface and an inline-start bar, never by colour alone. `<NavItem href="#x" current>Text</NavItem>` renders the anchor itself (`aria-current="page"` when `current`): for plain links and presets, where a compose tree can hold only manifest components; router apps keep passing their own link as the child.
- `<NavGroup label open onOpenChange>` is **controlled-only**, like Tabs: `open` and `onOpenChange` are required and it never opens itself. It renders a `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>` over a `<ul>` that is `hidden` when closed, so `aria-controls` always resolves. The chevron is `aria-hidden` and turns on a duration token.
- Tokens `--psi-nav-tree-*` alias the semantic layer, so under a `data-psi-theme="dark"` sidebar in a light page they resolve dark. The theme paints no background: the sidebar paints `--psi-bg-primary` itself.

## AppShell (D88)
- `<AppShell skipLink header sidebar sidebarOpen sidebarTheme>` is the **frame of an application**: a grid filling the viewport (`100dvh`) with the header in a row of its own over a sidebar and a `<main>` that **each scroll on their own**. Nothing scrolls under the header, so a focused element is never obscured by it (WCAG 2.2 *Focus Not Obscured*) — no `scroll-padding` needed, and none would work: measured on a `main` that is not the document's scroller, it does nothing. It is a **desktop frame**: no responsive drawer, no stored open state. A page whose document must scroll as a whole does not use it. Mount it at the root of the page with no margin or padding around it (it is `100dvh` tall, so anything around it makes the document scroll and slides the frame). Consult dist/patterns.json for the `app-shell` pattern.
- Slots: `skipLink` (a `<SkipLink href="#main">`, rendered first), `header` (a `<NavBar fluid>`), `sidebar` (a `<NavTree>`), and `children` as main's content. `main` carries `id="main"` (`mainId`) and `tabIndex={-1}`: the skip link's target, not a tab stop. The sidebar is a `<div id="sidebar">` (`sidebarId`), not an `<aside>`: the `NavTree` inside is already the landmark.
- `sidebarOpen` (default `true`) is **controlled**: wire your Menu toggle's `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls="sidebar"` and `sidebarOpen` to one piece of state. Closed, the sidebar is `hidden` (out of the layout and the accessibility tree, still in the DOM so `aria-controls` resolves) and `main` takes the full width.
- `sidebarTheme="dark"` sets `data-psi-theme` on the sidebar alone; its tokens re-resolve dark inside a light page, and the sidebar paints `--psi-bg-primary` itself (a theme paints no background). Tokens `--psi-app-shell-*`.
- `NavItem` takes `href` and `current` for plain links and presets: `<NavItem href="#sales" current>Sales</NavItem>` renders the anchor with `aria-current="page"`. A compose tree can hold only manifest components, so a preset cannot put a raw `<a>` in a `NavItem`; router apps keep passing their own link as the child.
- **Do not put a `ToastRegion` at `top-start` in an app with a skip link:** the native top layer paints over the focused link. Its default, `bottom-end`, is clear of it.

## Tabs family (4)
- `<Tabs value={v} onValueChange={setV} orientation="horizontal|vertical">` is **controlled-only** (D67): `value` and `onValueChange` are required, there is no `defaultValue`, and Tabs never selects itself. Compose `<TabList aria-label="…">` with one `<Tab value>` each, then one `<TabPanel value>` per tab.
- **Values are strings, not indices**, and `Tab`/`TabPanel` pair by value — their source order need not match, though keeping it matching reads better.
- **Activation is automatic**: arrow keys move focus and selection together. There is no manual-activation mode. Arrows follow the orientation's axis (Left/Right horizontal, Up/Down vertical) with wrap; Home/End jump to the first/last enabled tab; disabled tabs are skipped and use `aria-disabled`, not the `disabled` attribute.
- **Every panel renders; unselected ones get `hidden`.** So `aria-controls` always resolves and panel DOM state survives a switch. If a panel is expensive, render less *inside* it (`{selected ? <Heavy/> : null}`) rather than omitting the `TabPanel` — omitting it leaves the tab's `aria-controls` pointing at nothing.
- **A `value` that matches no tab** (an address naming a tab the user may not see) still leaves the list one tab stop: the first enabled tab takes it, or the first tab when all are disabled (D93). Nothing is selected, and development builds warn with the value. The selection stays yours; `Tabs` never picks one. A selected tab that is disabled keeps the stop, as before.
- `TabList` requires `aria-label`. The active panel is itself a tab stop, so a panel with no focusable content is still reachable.

## Menu family (3)
- `<Menu open onClose={(reason) => …} trigger={<IconButton …/>} placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end" aria-label="…">`: action menu on the native Popover API — top layer and light dismiss come from the platform, roving keyboard and dismissal reasons from Psi (D53). **Controlled-only** like Dialog: `onClose(reason)` reports `"esc" | "outside" | "item-select"` and the consumer flips `open`. Compose `<MenuItem onSelect>` and `<MenuSeparator>`; the trigger needs an accessible name, so an icon-only trigger is `<IconButton aria-label>`.
- Many menus, one state: for a row-actions column, hold a single `openMenuId` and render each row's Menu with `open={openMenuId === row.id}`, closing with `onClose={() => setOpenMenuId(null)}`. Do not give each row its own boolean. This is the shape D58 fixed a real dismissal bug in — switching directly between two menus left both closed, because the platform light-dismisses the first before the consumer's click handler runs.

## Compositions (recipes for what has no component yet)

- Form field: wrap the label, control, and message with `<Field label description error required>{control}</Field>` — label association (htmlFor/id), the description/error message line (swaps to error, aria-live="polite"; `announce={false}` drops the live region for an app that routes every announcement through one announcer of its own — the message still describes the control, D81), and aria-describedby/aria-invalid wiring onto a nested Input/Select are automatic (D49). `required` marks the label with an asterisk; `requiredText="(Required)"` states it in a word instead, the label's colour, aria-hidden because the control's `required` is the signal (D84). A control Psi did not write joins a Field with `const field = useFieldControl()` spread onto its focusable element — it returns `id`, `aria-labelledby` (a `<label for>` names only a labelable element, and a custom control is usually a div), `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid`, `aria-required` and `required` as the Field sets them, and `{}` outside a Field (D84); the element needs a role that admits aria-required, such as combobox. `group` mode renders fieldset/legend for self-labeled controls (Checkbox/Switch). Standalone Input/Select used outside Field still need `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` paired manually. Spacing: `psi-gap-24` between fields, `psi-gap-12` for toggle groups, `psi-gap-8` for button rows and label+Tag rows.
- Stacks/rows: `.psi-gap-*` utilities set only the gap — they do not create a flex/grid container. Pair them with `display: flex` (column for stacks, row for button groups).
- Page-level spacing: the form scale above (24/12/8) governs controls inside a form, not page layout. For layout use `psi-gap-32` between sections of a page, `psi-gap-24` between cards or panels in a grid, `psi-py-32` for a section's vertical padding, and `.psi-container` for the page's max-width and gutters (it is in utilities.css, not components.css). Marketing-scale rhythm is app-level and deliberately not tokenized — the system stops at the container.
- Utility classes: families are `psi-gap-*`, `psi-p-*`/`psi-px-*`/`psi-py-*`, `psi-m-*`/`psi-mx-*`/`psi-my-*` (all on the spacing scale), `psi-text-*` and `psi-display-*` (typography), plus `.psi-tabular`, `.psi-container`, `.psi-media-tint` and `.psi-sr-only` (hides content visually while keeping it in the accessibility tree). Scaled utility families set one property each and create no layout context — pair `psi-gap-*` with `display: flex`; the bare/fixed utilities (`.psi-container`, `.psi-media-tint`, `.psi-sr-only`) set several. Use `psi-m-0` to kill a UA margin rather than an inline style. The exact roster is `@handamade/psi-tokens/guidance.json` → `utilities.classes`.
- Native pass-through: components spread unlisted props onto their underlying element (Input → `<input>`, Select → `<select>`, Button → `<button>`/`<a>`), so `value`, `onChange`, `type`, `id`, `autoComplete`, `checked` etc. all work even though manifest.json lists only the component-specific props. Exception: Tooltip takes no host props — put handlers/attributes on its trigger child.
- Theming, programmatic: the standard setup is `data-psi-theme` on `<html>`. From JS, set it once at app init: `document.documentElement.dataset.psiTheme = "dark"` (React: in a root-level effect). Theme CSS does NOT paint the page background — paint `background: var(--psi-bg-primary)` at your app root yourself. For a themed subtree, set `data-psi-theme` on a wrapper and paint its background the same way; brand font combos do not reach nested subtrees (see guidance.fonts.scope).
- Size selection: 32 is the default (compact UI); 40 for comfortable forms and marketing pages; 24 for inline/table-row actions; 48 for hero CTAs.
- Tags & the accent rule (D40): Tags are passive labels — they do NOT count against "one accent per visual group" (that rule governs buttons/CTAs). Badge mapping: highlight (e.g. a plan badge) → `accent-subtle`; meta → `neutral-subtle`; status → `success`/`warning`/`danger`. On Tag, `subtle` is a boolean prop — `accent-subtle` is spelled `variant="accent" subtle` (Tag's variant union has no `-subtle` entries).
- CSS import order: all DS stylesheets are order-independent — base.css opens with an explicit `@layer psi.base, psi.theme, psi.components, psi.utilities;` statement. Recommended listing for readability: base → theme → components → utilities → @handamade/psi-react/styles.
- Widths: content widths are app-level; the system tokenizes the page container only (`--psi-container-max`). Dialog is the first component with its own width union — `width` is `400 | 560 | 720` (default 560).
- Full semantic token roster: `@handamade/psi-tokens/resolved/<theme>.json` has every token with resolved values — this file lists only the patterns.

Live MCP access to this data: see packages/mcp/llms.txt (hosted: https://psi.kurkin.de/mcp).
